A waterfront with memory

The Costanera is a way of looking at the city.

On the banks of the Paraná River, Costanera General San Martín connects an open horizon with plazas, recreation areas and places to pause. It is one of the most representative public spaces in Corrientes Capital and a regular meeting point for residents and visitors.

Costanera Norte was developed between 1929 and 1954 and extends for about 2.5 kilometres. Along its walkable waterfront are recognisable points such as Punta San Sebastián, Punta Tacuara and Parque Cambá Cuá, as well as views towards General Belgrano Bridge.

This is not an enclosed venue or a packaged excursion: it is a living urban edge, best experienced by noticing the river, the weather and the local pace.
Practical information

Before you go: the essentials.

This is an outdoor public promenade. The experience changes with the time of day, temperature, river level and events; check official channels for specific beach or activity information.

Fees and access

There is no general admission fee to walk the avenue and its public spaces. Beaches, events or temporary services may operate under their own rules and schedules.

When to go

Late afternoon pairs a walk and river views with less direct sun. For walking or cycling, avoid peak heat and bring water.

Parking

There are urban stopping and parking areas on nearby streets. Follow current signs, access rules and restrictions; do not obstruct pavements, cycle routes or entrances.

History of the promenade

Construction, extension and riverbank.

1929–1954

Costanera Norte construction

The stretch associated with Avenida General San Martín was consolidated across these decades as an urban riverbank project.

2008

Juan Pablo II extension

The city added approximately 900 additional metres of waterfront, expanding its recreational continuity along the river.

Today

A shared landscape

The wider waterfront connects promenades, beaches, green areas, monuments, panoramic points and everyday social life.

Suggested route

A mindful walk, not a race.

  1. Start with the river

    Choose an access near Avenida Costanera General San Martín and take a few minutes to orient yourself: wind, light and pedestrian flow set the pace.

  2. Follow the waterfront

    Walk at your own speed. The value of the route lies in shifting perspectives: trees, steps, rest points and the Paraná horizon.

  3. Add a green pause

    Parque Cambá Cuá and nearby spaces transition between the waterfront and the city fabric. Respect facilities, play areas and other people’s quiet time.

  4. Finish at sunset

    Low light makes the river’s breadth and the bridge silhouette stand out. After dark, choose illuminated and well-used sections.

Suggested route

A mindful walk, not a race.

Care for the setting

The waterfront is a shared place. Take your rubbish with you, respect emergency access, check bathing conditions if beaches are open and follow municipal guidance during high water, storms or large events.

Getting here

From the city, airport or bus terminal.

From the airport

Doctor Fernando Piragine Niveyro International Airport is outside the city centre. The municipality announced a dedicated airport–port bus in 2022; because services can change, check current transport before travelling. Taxi, remis or a pre-booked transfer are common alternatives.

By city bus

Stops and routes change with local operations. Consult municipal channels or the local operator to identify the route and stop best suited to your chosen access point.

Taxi, remis, bike or on foot

From the centre, the Costanera is reachable depending on the section you choose. Arrange drop-off at a clear landmark, use a helmet when cycling and cross only at marked locations.

Planning note: check current public city sources for timetables, fares and diversions. The municipal airport-service notice documents a historical route and does not guarantee present operation. Read the municipal notice.

Frequently asked questions

Answers for a better prepared visit.

Is there an entrance fee for Costanera Corrientes?

The general promenade is public space and has no general admission fee. Activities, open beaches or events may set specific conditions.

How much time should I allow?

Allowing between one and a half and three hours lets you walk, pause, observe the river and connect with nearby spaces. Actual time depends on the stretch, weather and mobility.

What is the best time to visit?

Sunset is popular for light on the Paraná and typically gentler temperatures. A morning visit can also be a quieter choice.

Are parking and restrooms available?

There are urban parking options nearby, subject to signs. Restrooms and other facilities should not be assumed across every stretch; verify on site.

Can I use public transport from the airport?

The municipality reported a dedicated service in 2022, but routes may change or be discontinued. Confirm the current position before planning and consider taxi, remis or a pre-booked transfer.
